summary: Linda Jean LaMacchia is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2001) under the supervision of David M. Knipe.
Linda Learman works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She conducted doctoral studies under Robert P. Weller and postdoctoral work under Peter N. Gregory (both attested 2005).
Linda Penkower is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed her PhD at Columbia University in 1993. She served as a research fellow at Taisho University (attested 1983).
Lindsay G. McCune is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She completed an MA under the supervision of Bryan J. Cuevas and studied under teachers Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan.
Lindy Li Mark is an anthropologist and Sinologist. She served as a professor of anthropology at California State University, Hayward, and at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Ling Ji is a Sinologist who completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisor Yuet Keung Lo.

Linnart Mäll (1938–2010) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1957–1962) and under Bidia Dandaron (~1966–1972), later holding a post at the University of Tartu (~1969–2010).

Lionel David Barnett (1871–1960) was an Indologist educated at the University of Liverpool and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held posts at the British Museum (1899, 1908–1936, 1948), University College London (1906–1917), and SOAS University of London (1917–1948).

Lionel Obadia is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from Lille University of Science and Technology in 1997. He held positions at INALCO, KU Leuven, Lille 3 University, EPHE, and Lumière University Lyon 2.

Lirong Qiu is a computer science scholar who earned an M.Sc. (2004) and Ph.D. (2007) at the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Qiu served as an associate professor of computer sciences at Minzu University of China (attested 2014–2015).

Lisa Grumbach is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held posts at Stanford University (attested 1996) and at the Institute of Buddhist Studies as an assistant professor.
Lisa N. Owen is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin under Janice Leoshko, and also studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995.
Lita Peipina is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed an MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under supervisor Jens Braarvig, and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Litian Fang (1933–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. After studying at Peking University (~1956–1961) under Feng Youlan, Yongtong Tang, and Zhang Dainian, he served as a professor, doctoral supervisor, and founding director at Renmin University of China (~1961–2014).

Liu Liqian (1910–2008) was a scholar in Tibetology. He held posts at West China Union University (~1944–1947), the State Council translation administration department (~1952–1959), and the Ethnic Publishing House (~1959–1982).

Lloyd W. Pflueger is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned a doctorate from the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Munich (~1969–1974).

Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso and served as Head of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (~1973–1997).

Lobsang Jamspal is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Columbia University under Alex Wayman. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, the University of Delhi, and Columbia University.

Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Drubwang Shakya Shri.
